sentence_stem: Left alone in the empty house,
correct_completion: she listened to the clock ticking in the hallway.
full_sentence: Left alone in the empty house, she listened to the clock ticking in the hallway.
acceptable_variants: she heard the clock ticking in the corridor.
she sat listening to the clock in the hallway.

options.text: the clock was left alone in the house.
options.why_wrong: The participle 'left' would then refer to the clock, but the sentence requires the implied subject of the participle to be the person who was alone.

options.text: to listen to the clock ticking.
options.why_wrong: An infinitive phrase cannot function as the main clause that completes the sentence.

options.text: she listened to the clock ticking in the hallway.
having listened to the clock earlier.
options.why_wrong: The perfect participle would describe an action completed before the situation in the stem, which conflicts with the simultaneous state of being alone.

grammar_focus: Participle clauses with an implied subject
explanation: A participle clause at the start of a sentence shares its implied subject with the main clause, so the main clause must describe what the person in the stem does.
translation: Pozostawiona sama w pustym domu, słuchała tykania zegara na korytarzu.
